sentences.text:
The learned Magistrate referred the complaint to the police for investigation under Section 156(3)
of Cr.P.C.
The police after investigation submitted the 'B' report to the learned Magistrate stating that the dispute between the parties is purely civil in nature.
Respondent No.1 filed a protest petition to the 'B' report submitted by the police.

The learned Magistrate after recording the sworn statement, rejected the 'B' report and registered the case against the petitioners/accused for the offence punishable under Section 415, 340, 305, 420, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.
Hence, this petition.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners/accused submits that the learned Magistrate without passing the order rejecting the 'B' report, at the first instance, has passed the order simultaneously rejecting the 'B' report and taken cognizance which is impermissible in view of the decision of the co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Dr. Ravikumar vs. Mrs. K.M.C. Vasantha and another, ILR 2018 KAR 1725.
4.

entities.text: Dr. Ravikumar vs. Mrs. K.M.C. Vasantha and another, ILR 2018 KAR 1725
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.1 submits that the protest petition and also the material produced along with the sworn statement clearly discloses the commission of the offences alleged against the petitioners/accused, and the learned Magistrate has rightly taken cognizance of the aforesaid offences, and the same does not warrant any interference.
5. I have examined the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.

6. The allegation against the petitioner is that the complainant and her children were taken to the office of the Sub-Registrar to execute the registered agreement of sale by paying an advance sale consideration of Rs.2 lakh and accordingly, she was an impression that she had executed an agreement of sale and thereafter when the complainant demanded to pay the balance sale consideration by executing the registered sale deed.
At that point of time, the petitioner stated that the sale deed having been executed, there is no question of paying balance sale consideration.
It is alleged that the sale deed was executed by undue influence and coercion .
7. To constitute an offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC, there must be dishonest intention from the very beginning, which is sine qua non to hold guilty of the petitioner.

In the instant case,
there is no allegation in the complaint that from the inception of execution of the agreement of sale,
there was dishonest intention on the part of the accused to cheat the complainant.
In the absence of essential ingredients, the cognizance taken for the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC is improper.
Even otherwise, the complainant has not taken any steps by the jurisdictional Civil Court to declare the sale deed executed in favor of the petitioner - accused was obtained by fraud.

8. The learned Magistrate was required to reject the 'B' report at the first instance, and thereafter record the sworn statement and take cognizance as held by the co-ordinate bench of this Court in the case of Dr. Ravikumar vs. Mrs. K.M.C. Vasantha and another supra.
